# Neurobiological

## Synthesis

The "Neurobiological" topic captures a cluster of findings about the biological basis of [[adhd|ADHD]], describing how brain structure and chemistry are thought to underlie the disorder's core symptoms. Across the corpus, this theme centers on two mutually reinforcing lines of evidence: altered neurotransmitter activity in specific brain regions, and delayed brain maturation.

A recurring claim is that part of ADHD's core symptoms can be explained by altered function in the brain's frontal lobes, caused by a relative deficit of the transmitter substances dopamine and noradrenaline in the synaptic clefts [^src2] [^src1]. This same source material also documents dysfunction corresponding to the parietal lobes, basal ganglia, and cerebellum, along with signs of an abnormal neurophysiological response to stress [^src1]. In other words, the neurobiological picture of ADHD extends beyond the frontal lobes alone, implicating a broader network of brain regions involved in attention, movement regulation, and stress response.

A second consistent finding is delayed maturation — specifically delayed myelination — of the cerebral cortex, documented in the source material [^src2] [^src1]. Myelination is the process by which nerve fibers become insulated, improving the speed and efficiency of signal transmission; a documented delay in this process offers one biological explanation for why ADHD symptoms often present as developmental in nature.

The corpus also situates these neurobiological findings within a wider causal picture: there is not yet full clarity on the etiology behind ADHD, but many factors are understood to contribute, among which the genetic causal component plays a significant role [^src1]. This framing suggests that the neurotransmitter deficits, regional brain dysfunction, and delayed cortical myelination described here are best understood as part of a multifactorial cause, rather than a single isolated mechanism, with genetics forming a significant contributing strand alongside the neurobiological findings.

## Claims

**Source: wikis/rkkp-adhd/raw/ADHD_2023.pdf, pages 41-45**
- En del af kernesymptomerne kan forklares ved en ændret funktion i hjernens frontallapper på grund af et relativt underskud af transmitterstofferne dopamin og noradrenalin i synapsespalterne [^src2] (Page 41)
- Der er dokumenteret en forsinket modning (myelinisering) af hjernebarken [^src2] (Page 41)

**Source: wikis/rkkp-adhd/raw/ADHD_2024.pdf, pages 56-60**
- Der er ikke fuld klarhed over ætiologien bag ADHD, men der er tale om mange faktorer, hvoraf den genetiske årsagskomponent spiller en væsentlig rolle [^src1] (adhd) (Page 56)
- En del af kernesymptomerne kan forklares ved en ændret funktion i hjernens frontallapper på grund af et relativt underskud af transmitterstofferne dopamin og noradrenalin i synapsespalterne [^src1] (adhd) (Page 56)
- Desuden ses dysfunktion svarende til parietallapper, basalganglier og cerebellum samt tegn på en afvigende neurofysiologisk reaktion på stress [^src1] (adhd) (Page 56)
- Der er også dokumenteret en forsinket modning (myelinisering) af hjernebarken [^src1] (adhd) (Page 56)
